Copied to the clipboard. Other apps can read the clipboard — paste the words into your password manager now, then clear it.

The clipboard is readable by other apps. Prefer writing the 12 words on paper. If you copy them, paste them into a password manager and clear the clipboard afterwards. NoteZero clears it automatically after 60 seconds.

These 12 words are shown only once. They are the only way back into your vault if you forget the master password.
Write the words down in order and keep them offline. Anyone with these words can open your vault.

Your notes stay encrypted as they are. Only the key wrappers change. Your existing 12-word recovery phrase keeps working — rotating it is a separate action in Settings, and it is the only way to get a new phrase.
Vault reset. Your recovery phrase is unchanged — the one you already wrote down still works. Rotate it in Settings if you want a new one.
The new password does not meet the requirements below.
Not available on this device. Password unlock always works.
Enabled. Uses the Android Keystore; re-enrolling biometrics invalidates it.
Unlock with your fingerprint or face; the key stays in the Keystore.
The vault also locks immediately when the app goes to the background.
No network permission, no account, no telemetry. Notes are encrypted with AES-256-GCM; the vault key is wrapped with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256.
Vault information is available after unlock.
Changing it rewraps the vault key; your notes are never re-encrypted.
The two new passwords do not match.
Rotate the 12-word phrase if it may have been seen by someone else. The old phrase stops working immediately.
Write these 12 words down in order. This is the only time they are shown. The previous phrase no longer works.
